$comment: Rows a reviewer who teaches to this curriculum set after reading the official text beside the derived crosswalk; they win over the derived rows. Written by scripts/curricula/apply-review.js from the review files; `why` is the reviewer's reason.

K:scene-search.why: Finding every look-alike in a busy scene is visual discrimination; the child neither names shapes nor describes positions, so it is a readiness step for K.G.A.1, not the standard itself.

K:order-by-size.why: Ordering three to five objects by length or height is 1.MD.A.1 (order three objects by length); K.MD.A.2 only compares two objects, so seriation goes beyond it.

K:patterns.why: The K.OA domain is addition and subtraction and says nothing about patterns; the only Common Core standard on shape patterns that follow a rule is 4.OA.C.5, for which this is readiness.

K:one-to-one.why: Matching each object with a partner object pairs objects with objects, not with number names; it is the readiness step for K.CC.B.4.a and for the matching strategy of K.CC.C.6.

K:count-how-many.why: Writing the numeral for a counted set is also K.CC.A.3 (represent a number of objects with a written numeral), which was missing.

K:colour-by-number.why: Colour-by-number is numeral recognition; the child writes no numerals and represents no count, so it only prepares K.CC.A.3.

K:dot-to-dot-sequence.why: Joining dots from 1 practises the count sequence by ones (K.CC.A.1); only the sheets that start at 11 count forward from a given number (K.CC.A.2).

K:ordinal-position.none: Ordinal numbers (1st to 10th) are not in the Common Core State Standards for Mathematics at any grade.
K:ordinal-position.why: K.CC.B.4 is about cardinality (counting tells how many); ordinal position is a different idea and is not a readiness step toward it.

K:combine-groups.why: Putting two groups together and counting all is adding within 10 with objects or drawings (K.OA.A.2), which was missing.

K:take-away.why: Crossing out and counting what is left is subtracting within 10 with drawings (K.OA.A.2), which was missing.

K:count-on.why: The skill itself names 1.OA.C.5 as the standard it leads to; that readiness row was missing.

K:number-bonds-k.why: Finding the partner that makes ten is K.OA.A.4, which was missing.

K:mirror-image.why: Nothing in the Kindergarten Geometry domain concerns reflection; recognising a mirror image is readiness for line symmetry, 4.G.A.3 (the standard the grade 2 symmetry points already use).

K:fact-fluency-colour-code.why: K.OA.A.5 covers fluency within 5 only; the within-10 sheets are 1.OA.C.6 and fluency within 20 is 2.OA.B.2.

1:write-the-equation.why: 1.OA.A.1 is solving word problems with unknowns in all positions; writing the equation for a picture where all three numbers are visible is K.OA.A.1 and only prepares 1.OA.A.1.

1:patterns-missing.why: Mapped to nothing while K:patterns was mapped; completing a repeating pattern is readiness for 4.OA.C.5 (shape patterns that follow a rule), the same as the Kindergarten point.

1:ordinal-numbers.none: Ordinal numbers and ordinal words are not in the Common Core State Standards for Mathematics at any grade.
1:ordinal-numbers.why: The Counting and Cardinality domain has no ordinal content, and grade 1 work cannot be readiness for a Kindergarten domain.

1:number-line-placement.why: Locating whole numbers on a number line with equally spaced points is the first part of 2.MD.B.6, which was missing (the grade 2 number-line point already uses it).

1:odd-even-pairs.why: Deciding odd or even by pairing objects and checking for a leftover is exactly what 2.OA.C.3 asks; it was marked readiness only because of the grade, while the same skill in K is marked teaches.

1:bar-model.why: Nothing in the skill reaches within 100 or two-step problems; the part-part-whole and comparison bar is the drawing of 1.OA.A.1 and a readiness step for 2.OA.A.1.

1:fluency-within-20.why: Adding and subtracting within 20 mentally and fluently is the wording of 2.OA.B.2, which was missing.

1:check-answers.why: 2.NBT.B.9 asks children to explain why strategies work using place value; marking worked sums right or wrong is not that, it is the true/false judgment of 1.OA.D.7.

1:bar-graphs.why: Bar graphs are named first in 2.MD.D.10 (draw a single-unit-scale bar graph for a data set); colouring a bar graph from counts is that standard, which was missing.

1:tens-and-ones.why: 2.NBT.A.3 is about numbers to 1000; expanded form of two-digit numbers is a readiness step for it (as the number-words point is already marked).

1:skip-counting.why: 1.NBT.A.1 is counting by ones to 120 and says nothing about skip-counting; counting by tens is K.CC.A.1 and by fives and tens is 2.NBT.A.2.

1:open-number-line.why: Showing sums and differences within 100 on a number line is 2.MD.B.6, which was missing; nothing in the skill reaches within 1000, so 2.NBT.B.7 is prepared, not taught.

1:bonds-to-100.why: 1.NBT.C.6 is limited to multiples of 10 in the range 10-90; partners of 100 (100 minus 30) go beyond that range, so the relation is extends.

2:hundreds-chart-moves.why: 2.NBT.B.8 is about numbers 100-900, which a hundreds chart never reaches (prepares only); moving by tens and ones to find a number or count the jumps is the place-value strategy of 2.NBT.B.5.

2:expanded-form-digit-value.why: The value of a digit in a three-digit number is 2.NBT.A.1, which was missing.

2:solids-in-real-life.why: Matching a real object to the solid it is shaped like is K.G.A.1 (describe objects in the environment using names of shapes), the most exact standard, which was missing.

2:read-jugs.why: 3.MD.A.2 names liters only; milliliters first appear in 4.MD.A.1 (relative sizes of l and ml), which reading a jug to 1000 and 2000 ml prepares.

2:choose-units.why: 2.MD.A.1 is about choosing and using measuring tools, not units; judging whether centimeters or meters, inches or feet fit is the unit sense of 2.MD.A.3 (estimate lengths in those units).

2:equal-groups-times.why: Writing the multiplication sentence for equal groups is 3.OA.A.1 (interpret a product as groups of objects), which was missing; 2.OA.C.4 stops at repeated addition.

2:arrays.why: Matching an array to a multiplication is 3.OA.A.1, which was missing; 2.OA.C.4 only asks for a sum of equal addends.

2:symmetry-line.why: Deciding whether a line is a mirror line and picking the symmetric picture is what 4.G.A.3 asks (recognise a line of symmetry, identify line-symmetric figures); it was marked readiness only because of the grade.

2:symmetry-complete.why: Drawing the missing half of a figure is not a readiness step: it goes beyond 4.G.A.3, which only asks to recognise and draw lines of symmetry.

3:estimate-by-rounding.why: Rounding the addends to the nearest 10 or 100 is 3.NBT.A.1, which was missing.

3:thermometer.why: Reading a temperature off a scale is not yet representing weather data in tables and graphs (3-ESS2-1); in mathematics the nearest standard is reading a scaled graph, 3.MD.B.3. Both are prepared, neither is taught (the mathematics reviewer's note, applied by the builder's own audit).

3:mult-div-relationship.why: Finding an unknown factor in an equation relating three numbers is 3.OA.A.4, which was missing.

3:balance-equations.why: The meaning of the equal sign is 1.OA.D.7; 3.OA.A.4 covers equations relating three numbers, so an equation with an operation on both sides goes beyond it.

3:time-12-24.none: 24-hour time is not in the Common Core; 2.MD.C.7 and 3.MD.A.1 use the 12-hour clock with a.m. and p.m. only.
3:time-12-24.why: 2.MD.C.7 is telling time to five minutes with a.m. and p.m.; converting between 12-hour and 24-hour notation is not what it asks.

3:equivalent-fractions.why: The parent standard also covers comparing fractions; recognising equivalent fractions as the same amount is exactly components 3.NF.A.3.a and 3.NF.A.3.b.

K:pre-writing-strokes.why: Pre-writing strokes are the readiness step for printing letters; the handwriting standard was missing.

K:beginning-sounds.why: Sorting pictures by beginning sound is also isolating the initial phoneme; RF.K.2.d was missing.

K:vowels-consonants.why: Telling vowel letters from consonant letters does not yet associate long and short sounds with vowel spellings; it is a readiness step.

K:segment-phonemes.why: Segmenting a word into its complete sequence of sounds is exactly RF.1.2.d; RF.K.2.d only isolates the first, middle and last sound of CVC words.

K:cvc-build.why: Building and completing CVC words from letters is phonetic spelling (encoding); L.K.2.d was missing.

K:digraphs-k.why: Kindergarten phonics names no digraphs; hearing sh/ch at the start is initial-sound isolation and a readiness step toward the grade 1 digraph standard.

K:word-sentence-tracing.why: The skill explicitly practises spaces between words; the print-concept standard RF.K.1.c was missing.

1:spell-picture-words.why: RF.1.3 is a decoding (reading) standard; spelling words belongs to the L.1.2 spelling components.

1:syllables-split.why: Clapping and counting syllables is the spoken-syllable standard RF.K.2.b, which was missing.

1:alphabetical-order.why: "L.1" is a whole strand, not a standard; ABC order is not named in Common Core and is the readiness step for using beginning dictionaries and glossaries.

1:articles.why: The exact lettered component for articles (determiners) exists; the general L.1.1 was used.

1:cloze.why: Choosing the word that fits a sentence is using sentence-level context (L.1.4.a), not general grammar (L.1.1).

1:question-words.why: Choosing and matching question words does not yet produce interrogative sentences; L.1.1.j is a later step, not taught here.

1:story-sequencing.why: Ordering pictures and sentences is not writing a narrative; it is a readiness step toward W.1.3.

1:word-classes.why: L.2.1.e is about choosing between adjectives and adverbs (wrong standard) and L.1.1 is too general; nouns/verbs and adjectives have their own components, and naming word classes leads to L.3.1.a.

2:sentence-boundaries.why: The capital-letter standard (L.K.2.a) was missing, and splitting run-together sentences is the readiness step for the run-on standard L.4.1.f.

2:cursive-writing.why: Common Core handwriting stops at printing all letters; cursive goes beyond that standard on the same line and was left unmapped.

2:describe-a-picture.why: Sentences from starters and a word bank are sentence production, not yet an informative text with a topic, developed points and a conclusion.

2:word-classes.why: The code named nouns, verbs and adjectives but only the noun component was read; L.2.1 is too general, and sorting by word class leads to L.3.1.a.

2:plural-nouns.why: L.2.1.b covers only irregular plurals; writing regular and irregular plurals together is the grade 3 standard L.3.1.b.

2:spelling-rules.why: Position-based spellings and ending rules are named word for word in L.3.2.f, which was missing.

2:read-cursive.none: Common Core has no standard for reading cursive script; RF.2.3 is about phonics and word analysis, not letter style.
2:read-cursive.why: RF.2.3 was attached only because the word 'read' appears; the skill is script recognition.

2:mystery-animal.why: Finding an animal from category and attribute clues is defining by category and key attributes (L.1.5.b), which was missing.

2:animal-fact-file.why: Gathering facts from a provided source to fill a fact file is exactly W.2.8, which was missing.

2:compare-two-animals.why: RI.2.9 compares two texts on the same topic; comparing the facts of two different animals practises the same-and-different step toward it.

3:cursive-sentences.why: Common Core handwriting stops at printing all letters; cursive sentences go beyond that standard on the same line and were left unmapped.

3:word-fields.why: L.3.5.c is about words for states of mind and degrees of certainty; telling apart closely related action verbs (stroll/dash, glance/stare) is L.2.5.b.

3:person-words.why: Knowing the meaning of a common derivational suffix (-er) is also RF.3.3.a, which was missing.

K:human-body.why: "K-LS1" is a whole strand and its one kindergarten standard is about survival needs; naming external body parts is a readiness step for the grade 1 external-parts standard.

K:living-nonliving.why: Telling living from non-living things is a readiness step; K-LS1-1 asks what living things need to survive.

K:fruit-vegetable.why: "K-LS1" is a whole strand; sorting foods into categories is L.K.5.a, and which plant part we eat prepares the grade 1 plant-parts standard.

K:seasons.why: The yearly cycle of seasons leads to the seasonal-pattern standards 1-ESS1-2 and 3-ESS2-1, which were missing.

K:natural-made.why: "K-2-ETS" is a whole strand and engineering design is not this skill; it is a category sort and a readiness step for classifying materials.

K:five-senses.why: "K-LS1" is a whole strand; the senses and their body parts prepare the grade 1 external-parts standard and the grade 4 senses standard.

K:plant-needs.why: That plants need water and light is investigated in 2-LS2-1, which was missing.

K:sink-float.why: "K-PS" is a whole strand and kindergarten physical science is pushes, pulls and sunlight; sink or float is a readiness step for classifying materials by observable properties.

1:animal-classes-coverings.why: 1-LS3-1 is about young resembling their parents (wrong standard); body coverings are external structures, which leads to 4-LS1-1.

1:life-cycles.why: Life cycles are the grade 3 standard 3-LS1-1; ordering stages does not itself compare young with their parents, so 1-LS3-1 is only prepared.

1:sink-float.why: Predicting and testing sink or float is investigating and classifying by observable properties (2-PS1-1); nothing is chosen for an intended purpose, so 2-PS1-2 is only prepared.

1:body-parts.why: Left unmapped, but naming external body parts is the readiness step for the grade 1 external-parts standard (same as K:human-body).

1:five-senses.why: The senses are asked for by name in 4-LS1-2, which was missing.

1:plant-parts.why: What each plant part does leads to the structure-and-function standard 4-LS1-1, which was missing.

2:materials.why: The grouping is done for recycling, so the reduce-human-impact standard K-ESS3-3 was missing.

2:plant-parts.why: What each plant part does leads to the structure-and-function standard 4-LS1-1, which was missing.

2:day-and-night.why: 1-ESS1-1 only observes the pattern; explaining day and night by Earth turning goes beyond it and prepares 5-ESS1-2.

2:habitats-adaptations.why: Naming a helpful body feature is a readiness step for the grade 3 argument about survival in a habitat, not that argument itself.

2:sink-float.why: The clay-boat task shows how the shape of an object helps it function, which is K-2-ETS1-2 and was missing.

3:water-cycle.why: "2-ESS2" is a whole strand; the exact grade 2 standard is 2-ESS2-3, which the water cycle goes beyond, and naming stages only prepares the grade 5 Earth-systems model.

3:planets.none: No K-5 NGSS performance expectation asks for the order or kinds of planets; the solar system is a middle-school topic, and grade 5 Earth-and-space standards are about star brightness and shadow/day-night patterns.
3:planets.why: "5-ESS1" is a whole strand, and neither of its two standards is about the planets.

3:investigation.why: Left unmapped although 3-5-ETS1-3 asks for planning and carrying out fair tests; the sink-or-float content goes beyond the grade 2 investigation standard.

K:transport-flying.why: No social studies standard exists here, but sorting transport into land, water and air is a category sort, which L.K.5.a asks for.

1:food-groups.why: No health standard exists here, but sorting foods into groups is a category sort, which L.1.5.a asks for.

K:grid-copy.none: Grid copying is a visual-spatial readiness skill; "K.G" is a mathematics strand and no ELA or NGSS standard asks for it.
K:grid-copy.why: It was mapped to a math strand that is not part of these two documents.

2:find-differences.why: One sentence per difference is sentence production, not an informative text with a topic and conclusion; the visual part has no standard.
